account:
Today I have been attending to ordinary municipal business while trying to understand a persistent, unusually vague rumour. The builder delivered the agreed visual bridge report and received the two-emerald fee. The crossing was passable on the builder's visits; the report neither certifies structural safety nor identifies repairs requiring authorization. At the ten o'clock mill inspection I observed two stacks of sixty-four hay bales and removed nothing. The secretary has acknowledged that observation but has no appointment book with them to confirm further inspection arrangements. I have returned to the town hall to check my remaining appointments; tea with my neighbour at the cottage is at three.

Several townsfolk have repeated essentially the same words, 'bridge or port change at bakery,' without supplying an identifiable event, an eyewitness, or a purpose. The secretary and neighbour have heard similarly vague talk and have not confirmed any change. The repetition is striking, but it does not establish that anything has actually changed, much less that people are conspiring. I did not find the baker in the bakery earlier. Now I can see the baker and freight near the west-bank bakery stall, both holding emeralds. That could simply be ordinary trade; I have not heard their conversation or witnessed a transaction. I want to ask the baker directly what, if anything, has changed. At present I cannot responsibly identify who is behind the rumour or what it is for.
